newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa aims to boost stainless steel output.
newsitem.headline: South Africa aims to boost stainless steel output.

text.p: South Africa will become the world's fifth largest producer of stainless steel by 1998, producing around 1.2 million tonnes of metal by 1998, a senior industry official said on Friday.

South African Stainless Steel Development Association (Sassda) executive director David Slater told Reuters, with global stainless steel production around 15 million tonnes a year, South African producers could become more important.
"We see South Africa becoming a very important player in the industry and what we believe is that we should encourage as much added value onshore as possible."
Slater said domestic demand for stainless steel was growing.
"The domestic market is growing very well, it will be over a 100,000 tonnes this year," Slater said.
He said South Africa's Columbus Stainless joint venture, one of the largest stainless steel facilities in the world which opened in February, had boosted the local manufacturing industry.
"I think they achieved the impossible. They commissioned a new plant which is four times as large as their (previous) facility and maintained production in a rising market," he said.
The Columbus plant is a joint venture between Highveld Steel and Vanadium Corp Ltd, Samancor Ltd and the state's Industrial Development Corporation.
The plant plans to produce 550,000 tonnes of stainless steel each year, most of which is destined for export.
Columbus has acknowledged that it had start-up production problems, particularly in the hot mill section. European buyers also returned several batches of aluminium slab because of poor quality.
But Slater said Columbus was working on the problems.
